# Critique — Pattern 1 (Cardiovascular)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed to prioritize high population-level information value: Diagnosed Conditions (~15%), Procedures & Interventions (~10%), Symptoms (~15%), Medications (~10%), Lifestyle & Risk Factors (~25%), Family History (~10%), and Monitoring & Self-Tracking (~15%). The last few monitoring questions (e.g., positions 252–255) felt slightly forced to reach exactly 255; had the limit been larger, more specific dietary and vascular sub-topics would have been explored. Overlap occurs with the Metabolic and Substances domains (e.g., smoking, cholesterol, blood pressure) because a reader holding only the Cardiovascular pattern needs a complete risk profile. The V-flag was applied systematically to questions where a "Yes" answer indicates a healthy/protective habit (e.g., regular exercise, home BP monitoring) to support a downstream convention where a stored bit `1` consistently indicates risk or condition presence. Some questions were inspired by the Rose Angina Questionnaire and AHA Life's Essential 8, which we paraphrased; clinicians seeking formal diagnosis should refer to official AHA or Rose Angina diagnostic criteria. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you feel that your cardiovascular health has improved...") due to its highly subjective nature. No prior questions existed for Pattern 1 in `patterns.json`, allowing this set to be drafted cleanly from scratch.
